title: Beyond Trial Averaging: Anchoring Neural and Visual Representations for Few-Repetition Brain-to-Image Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2608.19128v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decoding visual information from brain signals probes neural representations and enables neuro-rehabilitation and dream decoding. Recent brain-to-image retrieval approaches have achieved promising performance, typically by averaging many (up to 80) neural trials per image, requiring repeated stimulus presentation that increases latency, cost, and user burden. When only one or a few repetitions are available, the retrieval accuracy drops sharply. This drop is commonly attributed to query noise because averaging suppresses noise and increases signal stability. However, we find a non-transitive alignment pattern: the low-repetition query signal and the image representation each align with the high-repetition center, but not directly with each other. translated_title: 超越试验平均：锚定神经与视觉表征用于少重复脑到图像检索
translated_abstract: 摘要：从脑信号中解码视觉信息能够探测神经表征，并促进神经康复和梦境解码。最近的脑到图像检索方法通常通过对每张图像平均多次（最多80次）神经试验来实现良好性能，但这需要重复刺激呈现，增加了延迟、成本和用户负担。当仅有一次或少数几次重复可用时，检索准确率急剧下降。这种下降通常归因于查询噪声，因为平均能抑制噪声并增强信号稳定性。然而，我们发现了一种非传递性的对齐模式：低重复查询信号和图像表征各自与高重复中心对齐，但彼此之间并不直接对齐。这一模式表明，查询噪声只是问题的一部分，图库放置也影响检索效果。因此，我们提出了一种基于神经锚定的检索（NEAR）框架，该框架将神经锚定作为中间表示来改善少重复条件下的检索。
tldr: 本文提出NEAR框架，通过利用神经锚定作为中间表示，解决了少重复脑到图像检索中因查询噪声和图库放置引起的准确率下降问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the NEAR framework, which uses neural anchors as intermediate representations to address the accuracy drop in few-repetition brain-to-image retrieval caused by query noise and gallery placement.
